title: Electrospinning Fundamentals: Optimizing Solution and Apparatus Parameters
protocol: Choose a polymer based on specifications.
Select a solvent for the chosen polymer.
Choose suitable personal protective equipment.
Select a substrate based on application.
Choose collector geometry based on specifications.
Prepare several candidate polymer concentrations empirically.
Set up the electrospinning apparatus.
Load the syringe pump and set the speed.
Ground the collector.
Clip the high voltage wire to the conductor plate.
Start the wheel spinning.
Set the power supply to zero before turning it on.
Observe the stream while ramping up voltage slowly.
Adjust the voltage until a long and steady stream is obtained.
If a steady stream cannot be achieved, adjust the polymer solution concentration.
Use a dark matte backdrop for better visibility of the stream.
Place a unidirectional light source between the viewer and the stream.
Ensure the conductor plate contacts the needle tip properly.
Check that the collector makes contact with ground.
Increase the voltage if the drop at the syringe tip is leaning towards the wheel but not forming a stream.
Adjust the distance and voltage until a steady stream is visible for a 4% PLLA solution.
Remove large globs from the needle tip using a paper towel on a non-conductive stick.
Turn down the voltage or increase the distance between the syringe tip and the wheel when the stream is wagging up and down rapidly.
Increase the polymer solution concentration or add a little solvent with slower evaporation if the stream remains unstable.
Improve the length and steadiness of short or discontinuous streams by increasing the polymer solution, adding more slow evaporating solvent, and adjusting the voltage.
Ensure continuous contact between the conductor plate and the needle when beads are discovered in fibers.
Check that the grounded wire brush is making continuous contact with the wheel if fibers form as ribbons or bleed together.
Use a higher concentration of polymer or a solvent with a higher rate of evaporation for fibers forming as ribbons or bleeding together.
Increase the wheel speed or move the needle tip further from the collector when fibers form waves or curlicues.
Check that the conductor plate and collector are not vibrating if fibers are forming waves or curlicues.
Mix various polymer concentrations to observe the resulting streaming jets until a steady stream is obtained.
Decrease applied voltage if an oscillating or 'wagging' jet forms, which results in less well-aligned fibers.
Increase applied voltage if no jet forms and the solution only drips from the syringe tip.
Balance the distance between the syringe tip and the collector with the applied voltage to obtain a steady streaming jet.
